column1: # Runtime voice: lines that only exist in game, because they hold real values. Piper speaks them, no audio is built.
# Every .tsv in this folder is read, in name order. Add a row, or a file of your own, and restart KSP.
# UTF-8, tab separated, # starts a comment line. The columns are found by name: id kind when spanish english.
# This header explains them all. The other files in this folder use the same format.
# id       a-z 0-9 _, starts with rt_, unique over all files
# kind     report (now and then), dock (after a docking approach call), land (once per descent, low and falling),
#          science, science_pts (after a science reaction), contract_funds, contract_done, contract_failed
#          chat: an intercom chat between two kerbals. Id rt_chat_<name>_<seq>, one row per line, seq 1, 2, 3.
#          Kerbal A speaks the odd lines, kerbal B the even ones. Only line 1 has a when. A chat stays in one file.
# when     empty or any: always. A situation (orbit flight suborbital landed escape) and/or checks like fuel<25
#          or node_min>=2. Several situations: one must match. Every check must hold.
#          In a chat also the job of a kerbal: a=pilot (kerbal A, who starts) and/or b=scientist (kerbal B).
#          Jobs: pilot engineer scientist tourist. The chat only plays when the two kerbals have those jobs, in
#          either order: if only B has the job of a, B starts. A kerbal with a job from a mod fits no job check.
# spanish  normal Spanish. A number slot becomes Spanish words, reversed like every other word (loñapsE).
#          A name slot is spoken as the name. Write the number before a masculine noun: "un" for 1 is made.
# english  the subtitle. A number slot shows digits, a name slot the name.
# Versions: spanish and english may hold several versions split by |, in the same order. One is picked per play,
#   from the versions whose slots all have a value. Each spanish version uses the same slots as its english one.
#   Put lines with the same when in one row as versions. Give a line with another when its own row.
# Number slots: alt_km pe_km ap_km speed fuel day sci funds inc_deg period_min t_ap_min t_pe_min ec mono parts
#   crew node_dv node_min funds_total sci_total rep contracts dist_m close_ms height_m vspeed_ms
#   at_home flight_no missions stars visits landings (crew history, see below)
#   (km, min, deg, ms and sci get one decimal below 10, the rest whole numbers)
# Name slots: vessel body here exp target, kerbal in a report, and in a chat self (the speaker) and other (the one
#   spoken to). The same list is in src/Slots.cs.
# Crew history: in a report {kerbal} is the kerbal Mission Control talks to, and these numbers are that kerbal's.
#   In a chat they are the numbers of kerbal A (who starts). flight_no (this flight, 1 is the first), missions
#   (flights that ended with a recovery), visits and landings (earlier flights that reached or landed on this body),
#   stars (experience level). at_home is 1 at Kerbin, else 0. A template that uses them only plays with crew aboard.
# Avoid a plural noun after a value that can be 1: use a check like node_min>=2.
id
column4: spanish
column5: english

column1: rt_orbit
column4: Órbita estable. Periapsis {pe_km} kilómetros, apoapsis {ap_km} kilómetros. | Os vemos a {alt_km} kilómetros sobre {body}. | Seguimos vuestra órbita. Vais a {speed} metros por segundo. Nada mal. | Órbita confirmada. Periapsis a {pe_km} kilómetros.
column5: Stable orbit. Periapsis {pe_km} km, apoapsis {ap_km} km. | We see you {alt_km} km above {body}. | Tracking your orbit. You're doing {speed} m/s. Not bad. | Orbit confirmed. Periapsis at {pe_km} km.

column1: rt_orbit_inc
column4: Inclinación de {inc_deg} grados. Los de navegación están contentos.
column5: Inclination {inc_deg} degrees. Navigation is happy.

column1: rt_orbit_eq
column4: Órbita casi ecuatorial. Menos de un grado de inclinación.
column5: Almost equatorial orbit. Less than one degree of inclination.

column1: rt_orbit_period
column4: Una vuelta completa os lleva {period_min} minutos.
column5: One full orbit takes you {period_min} minutes.

column1: rt_orbit_tap
column4: Apoapsis en {t_ap_min} minutos.
column5: Apoapsis in {t_ap_min} minutes.

column1: rt_orbit_tpe
column4: Periapsis en {t_pe_min} minutos. Os avisamos.
column5: Periapsis in {t_pe_min} minutes. We'll let you know.

column1: rt_flight
column4: Altitud {alt_km} kilómetros, velocidad {speed} metros por segundo. Todo bien. | Os seguimos a {alt_km} kilómetros de altura. Seguid así.
column5: Altitude {alt_km} km, speed {speed} m/s. All good. | We have you at {alt_km} km. Keep it up.

column1: rt_sub_ap
column4: Apoapsis a {ap_km} kilómetros. Todavía no es una órbita.
column5: Apoapsis at {ap_km} km. Not an orbit yet.

column1: rt_sub_tap
column4: Llegáis a la apoapsis en {t_ap_min} minutos.
column5: You reach apoapsis in {t_ap_min} minutes.

column1: rt_landed
column4: Os tenemos en la superficie de {body}. Buen sitio. | Contacto con {body} confirmado. Bienvenidos.
column5: We have you on the surface of {body}. Nice spot. | Contact with {body} confirmed. Welcome.

column1: rt_escape
column4: Vais camino de salir de {body}. Velocidad {speed} metros por segundo. | Trayectoria de escape. {body} se queda atrás.
column5: You're on your way out of {body}. Speed {speed} m/s. | Escape trajectory. {body} is falling behind.

column1: rt_fuel
column4: Según nuestras pantallas os queda el {fuel} por ciento de combustible. | Combustible al {fuel} por ciento. Vamos bien.
column5: Our screens say you have {fuel} percent fuel left. | Fuel at {fuel} percent. We're good.

column1: rt_fuel_low
column4: Ojo con el combustible. Solo queda el {fuel} por ciento. | Combustible al {fuel} por ciento. Pensad bien la próxima maniobra.
column5: Watch the fuel. Only {fuel} percent left. | Fuel at {fuel} percent. Think hard about the next burn.

column1: rt_ec_low
column4: Batería al {ec} por ciento. Apagad algo, por favor. | Solo queda el {ec} por ciento de batería. Ahorrad energía.
column5: Battery at {ec} percent. Turn something off, please. | Only {ec} percent battery left. Save power.

column1: rt_ec_ok
column4: Batería al {ec} por ciento. Energía de sobra. | La batería está al {ec} por ciento. Todo en verde.
column5: Battery at {ec} percent. Plenty of power. | Battery is at {ec} percent. All green.

column1: rt_mono
column4: Queda el {mono} por ciento de monopropelente. Con calma con los propulsores.
column5: {mono} percent monoprop left. Easy on the RCS.

column1: rt_parts
column4: La nave tiene {parts} piezas. Esperamos que sigan todas ahí.
column5: The ship has {parts} parts. We hope they're all still there.

column1: rt_crew
column4: Contamos {crew} kerbals a bordo. Que nadie se esconda.
column5: We count {crew} kerbals aboard. No hiding.

column1: rt_day
column4: Día {day} de la misión. Aquí abajo todo en orden. | Llevamos {day} días de misión. Seguimos aquí.
column5: Mission day {day}. All fine down here. | That's {day} days into the mission. We're still here.

column1: rt_day_first
column4: Primer día de la misión. Ya sois famosos.
column5: First day of the mission. You're famous already.

column1: rt_vessel
column4: {vessel}, aquí Control. Os seguimos en pantalla. | {vessel}, os oímos alto y claro.
column5: {vessel}, Control here. We have you on screen. | {vessel}, we hear you loud and clear.

column1: rt_node
column4: Próxima maniobra en {node_min} minutos. Son {node_dv} metros por segundo.
column5: Next burn in {node_min} minutes. That's {node_dv} m/s.

column1: rt_node_dv
column4: La maniobra pide {node_dv} metros por segundo. Que no se os pase.
column5: The burn needs {node_dv} m/s. Don't miss it.

column1: rt_funds
column4: Contabilidad informa: tenemos {funds_total} fondos.
column5: Accounting reports: we have {funds_total} funds.

column1: rt_funds_low
column4: Quedan {funds_total} fondos. Volved con algo de valor.
column5: {funds_total} funds left. Bring back something valuable.

column1: rt_sci_total
column4: El laboratorio tiene {sci_total} puntos de ciencia. Quieren más.
column5: The lab has {sci_total} science points. They want more.

column4: Reputación en {rep}. El público tiene dudas.
column5: Reputation at {rep}. The public has doubts.

column4: Hay {contracts} contratos abiertos. Nadie dijo que fuera fácil.
column5: There are {contracts} open contracts. Nobody said it would be easy.
